blocks.text: Daniel pulled a fresh sheet of paper beneath the bench lamp. Beside it lay a handbill promising free electricity. He pushed Eleanor’s name under a coil of cable and began drawing.
Luke hovered above the opposite end of the bench. He had been waiting since the newspaper arrived.
“Are you going to tell me now?”
Daniel drew a circle. “The fish powered a robot big enough to overturn cars.”
“And they took him away.”
“I know what they did.” Daniel pressed the pencil harder. “But the fish was only carrying a fraction of the power. I was collecting from the wrong thing.”
Luke lowered himself nearer the page. “What thing?”
“That floating fireball with eyes.”
Luke remembered the little face burning above the street while he fought the glove. It had gone straight to the fish’s tank.
“He helped them.”

“He did more than that. Once he reached the tank, the fish stopped driving the robot.” Daniel tapped the circle. “We get him inside a collector, we draw the energy out, and we turn it into electricity.”
“Like the cage at the lake?”
“Something that can hold fire.” Daniel drew another line. “The cables and storage equipment will have to take far more than the old machine could.”
Luke watched the pencil move from the circle to a box, then out toward the edge of the sheet. Daniel kept adding lines. For the first time in days, he looked pleased with his work.
blocks.alt: In Daniel’s cluttered laboratory at night, Daniel points at a collector drawing while Luke’s floating blond head and iron jaws hover beside the workbench, his expression cautiously hopeful.

blocks.text: “That’s Skyfall?” Luke asked.
Daniel nodded. “Eleanor wants enough power to run Cleveland. Free electricity. She thinks it will get her elected.”
Luke’s iron teeth clicked softly. He steadied himself above the bench.
“So it’s for my body, too.”
Daniel reached for a ruler.
“You said you needed more power,” Luke went on. “That’s why I brought you the fish. If this one has that much more, you can put me right.”
“With that much energy, I could do work I’ve never been able to finish.”
Luke drifted closer. “Mine?”
“First I need the collector.” Daniel moved the ruler against the circle. “Then I need him in it.”
“How are you going to catch fire?”
“I’m working on that.”

Luke looked at the empty space beneath his jaw. He tried to imagine standing at the bench instead of floating over it. Shoes on the floor. Fingers resting on the paper. Walking out through the door without his uncle having to fix one more thing first.
“Tell me what you need,” he said.
Daniel glanced up at last. “Keep watch. Billy mustn’t see this.”
Luke moved toward the laboratory door. Behind him, the ruler scraped across the page and Daniel began another drawing.
This time, Luke told himself, there would be enough power. He stayed by the door, listening for footsteps.
